prologue.title: First Shift
prologue.synopsis: Meet the floor and Martha. Set the tone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Night one. The dispatch floor hums like a held breath — a wall of screens, a hundred blinking lines, and the quiet certainty that somewhere out there, someone is about to need you.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: You must be the rookie. Martha. Take the console next to mine — I'll keep you whole.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: One rule before the lines light up: not every voice on this frequency wants saving. Part of the job is learning the difference.

decision.prompt: First thing you say to your mentor

choices.label: I'm here to help all of them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha smiles like she already knows which kind of dispatcher you'll be. The first line lights up.

plot_call.title: The Call That Drops
plot_call.synopsis: A girl, an address, dead air. Martha says prank.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A young woman's voice, low and fast, like she's not supposed to be on the phone.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: Please — I'm at, it's the house on Calder, the blue one with the—

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The line goes dead. Not hung up. Taken away.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: Dropped call. We get a dozen a night off that block — kids daring each other. Mark it closed, rookie.

decision.prompt: The line just died. What do you do?

choices.label: Martha knows the block. Mark it closed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You write the address on a sticky note. Calder Street, blue house. Probably nothing. You keep it anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Straight to a dead tone — the line's been pulled. But the call's logged now, with a timestamp Martha can't quietly erase.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Closed: prank, juvenile. Martha nods, pleased. Somewhere a blue house on Calder goes quiet again.

weekend.title: Coffee With Martha
weekend.synopsis: The friendship deepens — the trap baits itself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha texts: 'Coffee? You look like the job's already eating you.'

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I mean it about keeping you whole. I burned out two rookies before you. I'm not doing it again.

decision.prompt: Martha, off the clock, being genuinely kind

choices.label: Let her in. She's good company.
Ask why she really chose this job.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She laughs at your jokes, pays for your coffee, and for one evening the city feels survivable. You almost forget the sticky note.

plot_call.title: Same Block
plot_call.synopsis: The pattern surfaces — and it traces back to Martha's console. The veteran is the villain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tuesday graveyard. A different voice. The same fear.

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: There's a house — girls go in, they don't, they don't come back out. I'm across the street, I can see—

lines.speaker: voice
lines.text: It's 1411 Calder. One door down from the blue one.

lines.speaker: mara
lines.text: I've got the nearest unit on a fender-bender two blocks over. Let me re-balance the board — I'll route this one when a car frees up.

decision.prompt: Martha wants to reroute the only nearby unit

choices.label: No — send a car to Calder now.
Note the address. Let her balance it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A unit rolls to 1411. They find a locked, empty house and an open back door — but it's in the system now. Same block, twice. You pull the dispatch logs to prove the pattern, and the pattern has a name: every unit that ever drifted away from Calder was rerouted from one console. Martha's. She isn't the burned-out veteran keeping you whole. She's the reason the street stays a blur.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By the time a car frees up, there's nothing to find. You add 1411 to the sticky note — two addresses, one street — and watch Martha close the ticket with a practiced flick. That's when it lands: she didn't balance the board away from Calder by accident. She's been doing it for years. The veteran isn't protecting the floor. She's protecting the house.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Martha handles it her way. The board balances, the street stays a blur — and you finally see the shape of it: the dropped calls, the rerouted units, the rookies she burned through before they could ask the wrong question. Martha was never looking out for you. She's the inside man, and tonight you helped her keep the door shut.
